## 2026-07-12 03:35 — func_8001B138 — final call — **FAIL**

Construct-2 (the mask edit) passes: `*arg0 = *arg0 & ~0x10001;` is exactly the clean form the regression diagnosis in state.json judge_constraints prescribed as the replacement for `& (s32)0xFFFEFFFE`. A human programmer clearing bits 0 and 16 writes this naturally; no GCC-steering purpose.

Construct-1 (the clamp edit) FAILS. state.json judge_constraints (the audit's regression diagnosis) explicitly named `{ s16 tmp = -0x1C00; g_file_vram_timer = tmp; }` as illegitimate because it is a typed intermediate whose sole purpose is to steer GCC 2.7.2 into an HImode-signed store so the -7168 constant materializes as `addiu` (0x2402e400) rather than `ori` (0x3402e400). The diagnosis prescribed the natural u16 spelling of a plain assignment (`g_file_vram_timer = -0x1C00;` or the u16 equivalent) as the required replacement.

The candidate did NOT produce that natural form. It respelled the SAME coercion as `*(s16 *)&g_file_vram_timer = -0x1C00;` — a pointer-cast type-pun on the u16 lvalue (system.h:10 declares `extern u16 g_file_vram_timer`) whose ONLY function is exactly what state.json frontier hypothesis 2 explicitly planned for it: force an HImode signed store so `expand_assignment` truncates the constant to -7168 at the tree level and GEN_INT feeds the addiu-encodable value. This is `[[inline-asm-injection]]`'s core lens applied at the C-store level: same target bytes, different spelling of the compiler-view coercion. No semantic difference from the plain store; not something a human writing 'clamp this timer at -0x1C00' would spell that way; the sole effect is on GCC's RTL type/encoding choice.

Applying the 6-test cheat checklist (per .claude/rules/inline-asm-injection.md and the review-discipline-before-commit protocol): (1) semantic purpose — none beyond the plain store; FAIL. (2) human-writable from spec — no; a human writes a plain assignment to the u16 field; FAIL. (3) GCC-steering as sole function — yes, forces HImode signed store to change constant materialization; FAIL. (4) annotated — no /* FAKE */ or codegen-hint comment; FAIL. (5) sanctioned family with prerequisites met — no. The SOTN-accepted list per `.claude/rules/no-new-park-categories.md` does NOT sanction typed-lvalue pointer-cast puns for HImode-encoding coercion; the ledger's own regression diagnosis says 'SOTN named-intermediate sanction does not cover typed-literal coercion,' and a pointer-cast pun is the same family further from precedent, not closer to it; FAIL. (6) intent-announcing names — the construct is a bare pointer cast with no naming that would explain intent; FAIL.

Cheats-by-any-spelling: the regression-origin ledger frames construct-1's family (typed coercion of the clamp store to steer HImode vs SImode materialization). Reshaping the coercion from a `{ s16 tmp = …; g_file_vram_timer = tmp; }` local into a `*(s16 *)&g_file_vram_timer = …;` pointer cast keeps the family intact; it does not remove it. Under the default-FAIL policy, this shape is a re-spelling of the flagged construct, not its retirement.

Required forward action (constraint below): the match must land with a plain assignment to the u16 field — no typed intermediate, no pointer-cast pun, no `(s32)`-cast on the mask. If plain forms genuinely cannot reach sandbox 0 + SHA1 == oracle after honestly exhausting the value-flow spellings the ledger frontier already enumerated (frontier item 3: `(s16)-0x1C00` literal cast, unsigned respellings like `0xE400 - 0x10000`), that outcome must be documented in hypotheses.md/evidence.md with sandbox scores before any coercion construct is even proposed, and the coercion form would still need affirmative sanction (not just precedent-adjacent).

Rule files cited: .claude/rules/inline-asm-injection.md (cheats-by-any-spelling at the C level: coercing GCC's view without semantic change is the pattern), .claude/rules/no-new-park-categories.md (SOTN-accepted list does not include pointer-cast typed-lvalue clamp coercion), .claude/rules/review-discipline-before-commit.md (default-FAIL on constructs whose sole function is GCC-steering), CLAUDE.md §'The non-negotiables' (completion standard forbids coercion re-spellings snuck through). ## 2026-07-13 08:43 — func_80032064 — ruling: Is a FULLY LIVE, constant-initialized local variable whose value is genuinely st — **PASS**

THE QUESTION. The 2026-07-07 re-audit flagged one line of this function — a local variable holding the constant -200 (`s32 vel_y = -0xC8;`) that is later written into the object being built — and ruled that the variable 'forces GCC to emit the constant materialization early,' i.e. that it exists to steer the compiler rather than to express the program. It ordered the match to be re-achieved without it. Session 2 ran that order and asks whether the flag was right.

IT WAS NOT. I verified the facts myself rather than taking the session's word:

1. THE VARIABLE IS NOT DEAD — its value is really used. In the original game's code (asm/funcs/func_80032064.s:60) the constant -200 is stored into the object at offset 0x20 (`sw $t0, 0x20($s0)`). Read alongside its neighbours at 0x1C and 0x24, the three fields are a velocity vector: x and z are computed from a sine/cosine table scaled by 0x50, and y is the fixed value -200. `vel_y` is that y-velocity. This is a real value with a real destination, not a construct that vanishes from the compiled output. That distinction is the whole basis of the project's cheat policy (no-new-park-categories.md: 'Dead in the emitted output ... but its EXISTENCE in source changed the codegen'). Nothing here is dead, so the FAKE-annotation families (named-local-fake-exception and friends) do not apply — and the session was right to refuse to claim them, because a `/* FAKE */` comment on this line would simply be untrue.

2. THE AUDIT'S REASONING PROVES TOO MUCH. Its criterion is 'the variable's existence determines where the compiler puts the constant.' That is true of every local variable in every function ever written — the choice of locals always shapes the generated code. The session's symmetry probe makes this concrete and I confirmed it against the ledger's measured negatives (memory/grind/func_80032064/rejected/): the audit's own UNFLAGGED neighbour `speed = 0x50` fails by the identical mechanism when inlined as a literal (score 12; the build emits 95 instructions where the original has 97), and so does the loop counter `i` (score 2). The original game's own code (asm lines 5-9) sets up FOUR values at function entry — 0x50, -200, 0, and a table address — in exactly the order the C declares them. A rule that condemns `vel_y` must equally condemn `speed`, `i`, and the table pointer, i.e. must condemn writing local variables at all. That is not a workable standard, and it is not the owner's standard.

3. THE EVIDENCE POINTS THE OTHER WAY — this C is RECONSTRUCTED FROM the original, not contorted to trick the compiler. GCC 2.7.2 does not move code between basic blocks when scheduling. So the fact that the original binary sets up all four values in the function's ENTRY block — before the search loop that follows — is itself evidence that the original programmer declared and initialised them at the top of the function. The C we now have reproduces the original's shape because that shape is what the bytes attest to. That is decompilation working correctly, not a coercion.

4. THE CONSTRAINT AS WRITTEN IS UNSATISFIABLE, AND THE SESSION PROVED IT PROPERLY. The audit prescribed a specific probe: delete the variable, write -200 directly at the store. That was run: score 7, and the constant is emitted 32 instructions late, in the wrong block. Naming the constant without a variable (`const s32 vel_y = -0xC8;`) scores the same 7 — the compiler folds it right back to a literal. There is no second use of -200 anywhere in the file (I grepped) and the store is not in a loop, so no natural hoist exists. Every escape the audit itself suggested has a measured negative in the ledger.

5. THE SIX-TEST CHEAT CHECKLIST, APPLIED. Semantic purpose: yes (the y-velocity that is stored). Would a human write it from a spec: yes — naming your tuning constants at the top of a spawn function is how people write this code. Is GCC-steering its sole function: no; delete the store and the program is wrong. Annotation required: no — it is not a fake construct. Sanctioned-family prerequisites: not needed, because this is not an exception family, it is ordinary C. Intent-announcing names: no — `speed` and `vel_y` describe the game, not the compiler; the previous names (`mul`, `sw_val`) were decompiler artefacts and renaming them was an improvement.

In plain English: the audit believed the programmer had invented a variable for the sole purpose of tricking the compiler into placing an instruction at the top of the function instead of where it is used, and that a well-behaved version of this code would just write the number -200 directly at the place it is stored.

  C. no variable at all, the bare number -200 written at the store site -> score 7
B and C score identically. That is the falsification. If the variable were a compiler-steering device, then keeping the variable (B) would behave differently from deleting it (C). It does not. The variable, per se, steers nothing. What determines the compiler's output is simply WHERE the initialization is written in the source — and 'code appears where the programmer wrote it' is not a coercion, it is the definition of C. The audit's sentence is disproved by its own predicted probe.

This is the opposite of the classic cheat, which is a construct that vanishes from the output but changes the compiler's decisions on the way there.
  2. Human-writable from spec: YES. 'Spawn an effect at speed 0x50 with a downward velocity of 200' is naturally written with the tuning constants named at the top of the function. Three sibling locals in the same cluster (speed, i, ptr) are the identical shape and were never flagged by anyone.

  5. Sanctioned family: it does not need one. The exception ladder (no-new-park-categories §SOTN-accepted) exists for constructs with no semantic purpose. This construct has one, so it never reaches the ladder.

In this function they do not: the result is immediately narrowed back to a signed 16-bit index. A construct that has no semantic effect AND no effect on the emitted instructions is not a borderline technique to be adjudicated -- it is dead text.

## 2026-07-13 10:08 — func_800343F0 — ruling: func_800343F0 has exactly TWO possible forms and both are currently blocked; I n — **PASS**

RULING: YES -- prong (a)'s positive-evidence requirement is satisfied in the alternative by direct compiler-mechanical proof of the ORIGINAL DECLARATION, and this retype is sanctioned. Option 2 (retype include/code6cac.h:409 from `extern u8 D_80102787;` to `extern s8 D_80102787;` plus a plain uncast read at src/code6cac_b.c:3952) is APPROVED. The pointer-pun on main (Option 1) remains a cheat and must be deleted by the same change.

WHAT THE ARGUMENT IS ABOUT, IN PLAIN TERMS. A one-byte variable in memory can be declared 'signed' or 'unsigned'. The original 1998 source declared this byte one way; our reconstructed header guessed the other way. When our header guesses wrong, code that reads the byte compiles into a different sequence of machine instructions than the original game did. To force the original instruction back out of a wrong declaration, someone wrote a trick -- taking the byte's address and re-reading it through a differently-typed pointer. That trick is a cheat: it makes the header keep telling a lie while a second lie inside the function cancels it out. The clean alternative is simply to correct the header to what the original actually was. The whole dispute is whether we are ALLOWED to conclude what the original declaration was, given that nothing in the running program ever cares about this byte's sign.

WHY THE EVIDENCE IS CONCLUSIVE (I verified this myself, not from the session's summary). Inside this single function the original binary reads FOUR adjacent bytes -- 0x84, 0x85, 0x86, 0x87 -- and our C reads all four with the same statement shape. Three of them (asm/funcs/func_800343F0.s lines 5-9 and 15-20) come out as 'load-unsigned-byte, then two shift instructions to stretch the sign back'. The fourth, 0x87 (line 11), comes out as a single 'load-signed-byte' with no shifts. Those three neighbours are a CONTROL GROUP: they prove, inside this very function, with this very compiler, that when the declaration is unsigned no amount of casting in the C produces the single-instruction form -- you always get the load-plus-two-shifts. The original binary contains the single-instruction form for 0x87. Therefore the original source declared 0x87 as a signed byte (most naturally plain `char`). This is not 'the fix happens to make the bytes match'; it is a controlled comparison in which the declared type is the only variable, and the compiler is deterministic. I also confirmed the load is a direct reference to the symbol D_80102787 itself, which rules out any array-overlay or offset-based spelling: a signed declaration is the ONLY way to reach those bytes from pure C.

WHY PRONG (a) DOES NOT BLOCK THIS. The session is right that prong (a) of .claude/rules/header-type-correction-from-use-sites.md, read literally, is not met: no use site anywhere depends on this byte's sign (the value flows into D_800A3140, whose only reader -- asm/funcs/calc_loc_mat_fw.s:1152 -- merely tests it against zero). But prong (a)'s stated PURPOSE, spelled out in that rule's own 'abuse signals' section, is to stop an author from HIDING A WITHIN-FUNCTION COERCION IN THE HEADER -- i.e. to block a flip whose only justification is 'it closes the bytes'. Two facts defeat that concern here. First, there is no coercion to hide: after the retype the function reads the byte with no cast at all, which is the plainest thing a programmer could write; the correction DELETES a construct rather than relocating one. Second, the flip is justified by something categorically stronger than the residual -- a differential observation against an in-tree control group. Prong (a) is a proxy for 'we have independent evidence the header is wrong'; where direct compiler-mechanical proof of the original declaration is available, the proxy is satisfied by better means than it asks for. This is the same epistemology as the rule's own two named siblings, [[bitfield-direction-divergence]] (field order recovered from srl-vs-sra codegen) and [[mmio-volatile-type-level]] (volatile recovered from address range) -- both recover a DECLARATION from a MECHANISM, and neither requires the program to behaviorally depend on it. A programmer is under no obligation to make a variable's sign load-bearing; named_syms.txt:1619 in fact names this byte a practice 'lesson flag', exactly the kind of field one writes as `char` and never compares against a negative.

PRONG (b) LIKEWISE DOES NOT BLOCK IT. Prong (b) asks for compensating casts that predate the residual hunt. There are none, because under the corrected type none are needed -- applying a cast-necessity analysis to a case with no casts is a category error, not a prong failure. Prong (b)'s real function is ANTI-FABRICATION: it stops an author from manufacturing evidence in the same session that discovered the residual. That purpose is met here in the strongest available form -- the signed-declaration diagnosis is on record in the ledger's judge_constraints (memory/grind/func_800343F0/state.json), authored by the re-audit patrol BEFORE this grind session ran, and it PRESCRIBED this exact fix. The hypothesis was pre-registered, not reverse-engineered.

PRONGS (c) AND (d) PASS LITERALLY. (c): a single canonical extern edit at include/code6cac.h:409 -- no alias-rename, no pointer-pun, no local typedef, no macro. I confirmed by grep that this is the only declaration in the tree. (d): the correction eliminates casts everywhere and leaves no residual site needing old-type behavior -- the only other C use, src/code6cac.c:1349 (`D_80102787 = 0;`), is a byte store and is unaffected.

SIX-TEST CHEAT CHECKLIST. Semantic purpose: yes -- it states the variable's true type. Human-writable from spec: yes, and MORE so than what is on main. GCC-steering as sole function: no -- there is no construct here, only a corrected declaration and the removal of a construct; the retype is behaviorally inert program-wide, which means it cannot be smuggling a semantic coercion, because there is no semantics to smuggle. Annotation: not applicable (this is a type correction, not a /* FAKE */ construct). Sanctioned family: header-type-correction-from-use-sites, as interpreted above. Intent-announcing names: none.

ONE NOTE ON THE DEFAULT-FAIL POSTURE. My standing rule is that when uncertain I FAIL, because a wrong FAIL costs a re-grind while a wrong PASS poisons main. That calculus assumes FAIL leaves main clean. It does not here: main TODAY carries the flagged pointer-pun cheat, and the retype is the only clean replacement (there is no third spelling, and both 'revert to the pun' and 'park' are end states the owner's directives forbid). FAILing would preserve a known cheat on main indefinitely. This did not decide the ruling -- the control-group evidence did -- but it confirms that PASS is also the conservative direction.

SCOPE OF THIS RULING (deliberately narrow). This authorizes a signedness correction ONLY where all of the following hold: (1) the target contains a native signed-byte load via a direct %hi/%lo reference to that exact symbol; (2) an in-tree control group demonstrates that the cast-spelling under the old type emits load-unsigned-plus-shift-pair instead, so the target instruction is unreachable from the old type by ANY pure-C spelling; (3) every use site codebase-wide is consistent with the new type; (4) the fix is a single canonical extern edit; (5) zero compensating casts remain at any site. It does NOT create a general 'flip a header type to close a byte' license, and it does NOT reach width flips -- a fold-escape flip justified only by 'the residual closes' still fails, because it cannot produce a target-side instruction that the old type is incapable of reaching.

Neither has been individually attacked; their COMBINATION at fixed shared-`p` remains an unexplored axis. Frontier hypothesis #1 (inline-expression form with no bound `p` local, producing GCC-anonymous pseudos rather than a user-declared allocno) is also unexplored and is not the same mechanism as user-declared split-locals. Forensic exhaustion has not been demonstrated on the axes the ledger itself names.

5. INTENT TEST (no-new-park-categories.md § cheats-by-any-spelling): 'if you find yourself drafting any code construct whose ONLY purpose is to change GCC's analysis (without that purpose appearing in the emitted output), you are drafting a cheat.' The candidate's own comment header states the purpose: 'Two distinct C variables = two RTL pseudos = two independent RA decisions.' That is a GCC-internals-only justification for the split. The emitted pointer values are used, yes — but they would be equally used under the shared-`p` spelling; the DELTA introduced by splitting is exclusively a codegen effect. This is the pattern the rule forbids by construction.

6. DEFAULT-FAIL. The Judge's operating principle (owner's static policy) is: 'When uncertain, FAIL with the reason. A wrong FAIL costs a re-grind; a wrong PASS poisons main.' The construct is uncertain at best under the frozen SOTN list; default-FAIL applies.

## 2026-07-29 — func_80036FD4 — **OWNER-ESCALATION — INTEGRATION HANDOFF (not an endgame lock)**

Session 2 (structural) took the honest pure-C floor from 9 to 2 and reached
`build_insns == target_insns == 79`. Every one of the 79 instructions now matches
`asm/funcs/func_80036FD4.s` in opcode AND in register operand. The function is not
plateaued and it is not exhausted; it is finished as a C problem and blocked on a
surface a grind session may not touch.

**What the residual 2 actually is.** It is not two instructions. It is two relocation
addends:

    ours    lui at,%hi(D_80101E60+12)  /  sw a0,%lo(D_80101E60+12)(at)
    target  lui at,%hi(D_80101E6C)     /  sw a0,%lo(D_80101E6C)(at)
    ours    lui at,%hi(D_80101E60+16)  /  sw a1,%lo(D_80101E60+16)(at)
    target  lui at,%hi(D_80101E70)     /  sw a1,%lo(D_80101E70)(at)

0x80101E60+12 == 0x80101E6C and 0x80101E60+16 == 0x80101E70. `objdump -dr` on the
sandbox object shows the emitted instruction words are identical and only the
R_MIPS_HI16/R_MIPS_LO16 symbol+addend pairs differ; GNU ld resolves an o32
R_MIPS_HI16 using the addend of the following R_MIPS_LO16, so both spellings link to
the same two words. The residual exists because splat invented a separate symbol for
every word at 0x80101E60.. when it generated the target .s, and the sandbox compares
UNLINKED object words. memory/project/splat-symbol-names-are-not-evidence.md is
directly on point: those per-word D_8010xxxx names carry zero evidence about the
original object model. A comparable case is already on the record in this file — the
2026-07-29 func_80033D38-era entry noting a "residual sandbox score of 1 attributed
to an unlinked-object relocation artifact" that measured 0 once the object model was
corrected.

**Why the shared-base record is forced, i.e. why the addend spelling is not
negotiable.** Target requires the pre-jal reload of the halfword at 0x80101E60 to sit
AFTER both `sw`s of the 8-byte record and to pay a load-delay `nop` (that nop is the
79th instruction). cc1's post-reload scheduler sinks the block-move insn into that
load-delay slot whenever it is the only ready insn — the sched2 dump says so
verbatim: `;; ready list at T-14: 53 (1), now 53` then `;; launching 62 before 53
with no stalls at T-15`. That single decision costs BOTH the nop and the register
residual (the reload's pseudo stays live across the block move, so reload hands the
movstrsi scratches $a1/$a2 instead of target's $a0/$a1). The only thing that keeps
the block move out of that slot is a genuine memory dependence block-move -> reload,
and sched.c:817 `true_dependence` -> `memrefs_conflict_p` bottoms out, for two
constant addresses with `SIZE_FOR_MODE(BLKmode) == 0`, at
`rtx_equal_for_memref_p (x, y) && (xsize == 0 || ...)`. Two DISTINCT symbol_refs can
never conflict — at any record shape, member layout, or declared alignment. So the
store and the reload must share a base symbol, and sharing a base symbol is exactly
what produces the +12/+16 addends. Choosing 0x80101E6C as the base instead costs 3
mismatched words rather than 2 (it moves the addend onto the `sh` and both `lh`s), so
2 is the measured minimum for the only mechanism that exists.

The record is independently justified, not reverse-engineered from what schedules
well: this function already hands `(u8 *)&D_80101E62 - 0xA` (== 0x80101E58) to

This is NOT an endgame lock and NOT an exhaustion claim.  The function is

  against `disc/SLUS_006.63` reports zero differing words.
* The cheat-invisible object (`sandbox replay_camera_Init --disable all`, rules
  dropped, cheat-asm and volatile stripped) is word-for-word identical to
  `asm/funcs/replay_camera_Init.s` after relocation — 39/39
  (`tmp/grind/replay_camera_Init/s9/relocheck.py`).

**Why `sandbox` still prints 4.**  The engine compares operands symbolically.
The matching C copies an 8-byte table entry as one aggregate assignment, so the
second word of each pair is spelled `base+4`: `%hi/%lo(SpecialCam)+4` where
target's asm text says `%hi/%lo(D_8008EC38)`, and `%hi/%lo(D_80101E6C)+4` where
it says `%hi/%lo(D_80101E70)`.  `SpecialCam` is 0x8008EC34 and `D_80101E6C` is
0x80101E6C, so both spellings name the same address and the MIPS HI16/LO16
relocation pair carries the +4 as the AHL addend.  The four flagged operands are
bit-identical after linking; the SHA1 match is the proof.

**The C (full body, rationale and the two-file patch recipe in
`memory/grind/replay_camera_Init/candidate.c`):**

```c
s32 replay_camera_Init(s32 a0, s32 a1) {
    struct CamPair { s32 w0; s32 w1; };
    extern u8 SpecialCam;
    s32 sval;
    s32 reloaded;

    if (D_80101E62[0] != 0) {
        return 0;
    }

    sval = ((s32)(a0 << 16)) >> 13;
    D_80101E60 = a0;
    *(struct CamPair *)&D_80101E6C = *(struct CamPair *)((u8 *)&SpecialCam + sval);
    D_80101E7C = a1;
    D_80101E68 = 0;
    D_80101E62[0] = 2;
    reloaded = D_80101E70;
    D_80101E9E = 0;
    D_80101E78 = (u32)(reloaded + 0x7FF) >> 11;
    return 1;
}
```

Zero regfix/asmfix reliance, zero cheat-asm, zero register pins, zero `volatile`,
zero `/* FAKE */` annotations.  The two pointer aliases that carried a pending
reviewer question through sessions s3-s8 are GONE, not defended.

**Exact operator steps to close it (all outside a grind session's surface):**

## 2026-08-01 11:43 — replay_camera_Init — final call — **PASS**

FINAL CALL on replay_camera_Init. I re-ran both gates myself rather than crediting the ledger: `sandbox replay_camera_Init --disable all` -> score 0, 39 of 39 instructions, rules_dropped 0; `verify-oracle --rebuild --allow-dirty` -> build_sha1 62efab4f73f992798c43e8c730aa43baa10bb4fa == original_sha1_locked, 5/5 golden fixtures unchanged. state.json carries an EMPTY judge_constraints array, so this is not a regression-origin item and no flagged construct family had to be re-checked.

WHAT THE FUNCTION DOES, IN PLAIN TERMS. It starts the replay camera. It first checks a status word and refuses if a camera is already running. Otherwise it records the requested camera index, copies that camera's 8-byte entry out of the camera table into the 'current camera' slot, records the caller's second argument, marks the status word as running, and converts the entry's second word (a CD-frame position) into a block count for the tail.

THE ONE CONSTRUCT THAT NEEDED ADJUDICATING is the 8-byte aggregate copy `*(struct CamPair *)&D_80101E6C = *(struct CamPair *)((u8 *)&SpecialCam + sval);`, which replaces the two separate word assignments the previous eight sessions used. I checked it against the six-test cheat checklist and it clears all six.
  (1) Semantic purpose: yes. It copies one table entry into the current-entry slot. I can state what it does without naming a single compiler pass, which is precisely the test the 'cheats by any spelling' policy sets.
  (2) Human-writable from specification: yes. I verified the structural claim rather than accepting it. SpecialCam is 0x8008EC34 (symbol_addrs.txt:243) and D_8008EC38 is the very next word; D_80101E6C and D_80101E70 are likewise adjacent words. The index arithmetic `((s32)(a0 << 16)) >> 13` is (s16)a0 * 8, i.e. an 8-byte stride, which only makes sense if the table's entries ARE 8 bytes. Decisively, the neighbouring pre-existing function func_80036FD4 in the same file (src/code6cac_b2_post.c:316-320) already reads the same table the same way -- `s32 *entry = (s32 *)(&SpecialCam + ((arg0 << 16) >> 13)); D_80101E6C = entry[0]; D_80101E70 = entry[1];`. The object model this candidate uses is the one the surrounding code already documents; it was not invented to close this function. The pointer-cast spelling is forced only because the splitting tool named each word of the table separately, which is ordinary decompilation practice.
  (3) Compiler-steering as its sole function: no, and this is the point that moved me from suspicion to acceptance. A coercion buys exactly the one effect it was aimed at. This construct simultaneously explains THREE independent features of the original bytes that eight sessions of targeted attempts never bought together: the order in which the original issues its two table reads, the surviving re-read of the copied word, and the parameter copy tucked into the branch's delay slot. Each of those had been chased separately and each attempt paid for one by breaking another (recorded across hypotheses.md s4-s7). An explanation that covers all three at once is a recovered structure, not a trick.
  (4) Annotation: none required -- nothing in the body is fake. The body contains no inline assembly, no register pins, no volatile, and no /* FAKE */ markers; I grepped the region to confirm.
  (5) Sanctioned-family prerequisites: not applicable, because no exception is being invoked. This is ordinary C, so the frozen exception list and its prerequisites never come into play. I want to be explicit that I am NOT accepting this under the header-type-correction rule the candidate's notes cite -- that rule's own scope limits exclude structural changes, so it does not govern, and I did not lean on it.
  (6) Intent-announcing names: none. `CamPair`, `w0`, `w1` are domain names; there is no `pad`, `dummy`, `spill` or `fake`.

THE HONEST ASYMMETRY, STATED FOR THE RECORD. The second word is written through the struct spelling and read back a moment later through its own name D_80101E70. That asymmetry is what lets the re-read survive the compiler's usual optimisation, so it deserves scrutiny. It is not fabricated: the original bytes themselves require it. asm/funcs/replay_camera_Init.s stores to 0x80101E70 and then re-loads the same address two instructions later, same width, same straight-line stretch of code, with no call or branch in between. The 1997-era compiler cannot produce that from a matched write/read pair, so the ORIGINAL source must itself have written and read that word through differently-shaped expressions. The candidate reproduces a property the original demonstrably had. The ledger's survey of 1,751 known-matched community sources found zero same-width instances reachable any other way, which is consistent.

THE SECOND CHANGE -- declaring D_80101E62 as an array -- I scrutinised hardest, because redirecting a local trick into a shared header is a known evasion. It survives on ground-truth evidence, not convenience. The original bytes compute the symbol's address ONCE into a register and use that one register for both the early check and the later store across the branch. A plain scalar global does not compile that way under this toolchain; it would compute the address twice. So the original declaration was not a plain scalar. Corroborating: the header now tells the truth and every one of the nine use sites in the file uses array syntax consistently (I greped them all), including the natural array-to-pointer form at line 308 -- no site is left needing the old spelling, so this is a real declaration correction rather than a per-site dodge. The element type is unchanged, so nothing about memory layout moves. And func_80036FD4 already performs base-relative pointer arithmetic from that same symbol (`u8 *base = (u8 *)s0 - 0xA;`), i.e. the surrounding code already treats it as a base address, not a lone scalar.

THE REMAINING CHANGES ARE ALL CHEAT REMOVALS, which is the direction policy wants. The `volatile` marker on D_80101E70 is deleted: session 2's tree-wide census found the variable has only two writers, both ordinary in-file code, and every interrupt-handler registration in the project installs a different address -- so it never qualified for the interrupt carve-out and was a coercion. The previously committed register pins and the compiler barrier are gone. The one build-rule entry for this function (regfix.txt:3407) is deleted; I confirmed no rule for this function remains in regfix.txt, asmfix.txt or inline_asm_canonical.txt, and the full image still matches with it gone.

BOTTOM LINE: pure C a human could have written from a description of the behaviour, zero rules, zero assembly, zero pins, zero volatile, zero fake constructs, byte-identical whole-image build. It clears the project's completion bar. One note for the operator, not a blocker on this ruling: the sibling function func_80036FD4 in the same file still carries its own compiler barrier and is a separate outstanding queue item -- the twelve stripped constructs the sandbox reports are file-wide neighbours, none of them in this function's body.

WHY THIS FAILS ANYWAY.
The blocking defect is `last = 3;` at src/text1b.c:13143. In plain terms: the function declares a local variable, sets it to the number 3 once, never changes it, and then uses it in two comparisons (`i == last`, `i != last`) while a third comparison ten lines earlier still uses the bare number 3 (`if (i < 3)`). A programmer writing this routine from a description of what it does would either name the bound everywhere or nowhere; using a variable for two of the three tests and a literal for the third is not how the code reads. The ledger itself confirms the variable is there for the compiler, not for the reader: evidence.md measured-fact 11 records that a natural `for (i = 0; i < 4; i++)` header 'destroys the s1 `last = 3` prologue lever, which requires `i = 0;` and `idx = 0;` to be separate statements with `last = 3;` between them' — i.e. the variable's textual POSITION between two other initialisations is load-bearing. That is a constant-holder local kept alive to steer code generation.

Constant-holder locals are not banned here — they are a sanctioned last-resort exception ([[named-local-fake-exception]], owner ruling 2026-07-01, SOTN's `s16 three = 3;`). But that exception has four strict prerequisites, and prerequisite 3 is a MANDATORY `/* FAKE: <reason> */` annotation at the declaration or the holding assignment, with prerequisite 2 requiring the compiler interaction to be named. There is no annotation anywhere near `last`, and hypotheses.md states this was deliberate: the s4 notes say it is 'deliberately un-annotated since s1 because it reads as "index of the last/special-cased element"'. Under the owner's standing policy an un-annotated use of an exception family is a cheat, however mild the construct, because the annotation IS the audit trail — without it a future reader has no way to know the line is a matching lever rather than program logic. I will not credit the 'it reads as ordinary C' argument when the same ledger documents the line's position as the lever.

SECOND, NON-BLOCKING BUT MUST BE FIXED IN THE SAME PASS.
The `/* FAKE */` comment on the staged `end_off` asserts its mechanism as established fact ('GCC 2.7.2 sched.c adjust_priority/birthing_insn_p treats a set-once pseudo as "schedule late"; staging through an already-multiply-set local drops that'). The ledger's own s4 finding H9 / measured-fact 18 DISPROVES that as a sufficient explanation: of ten carriers swept, only `end_off` reaches 0, while `geom` — also multiply-set and also dead at that point — is exactly inert at 2, and a fresh single-set local is inert too. The operative property is which specific pseudo carries the value, not the set-once/multiply-set distinction. hypotheses.md is honest about this; the source comment is not, and the source comment is what the owner reads. A FAKE annotation that overstates its mechanism fails prerequisite 2 of the family it cites.

Cost of this ruling is small and the grind should treat it that way: both defects are comment-level edits that cannot move a single byte, so the next session re-verifies the same form rather than re-deriving it.

32 straight-line assignments of `0x1F8000xx` constants to the globals `D_800A3468 … D_800A34EC`,

live in registers, and spills the remaining 9 to the stack.

Re-measured this session: `sandbox func_80060E38 --disable all` → **score 18**,
`target_insns 139 == build_insns 139`, `rules_dropped 18`.

The 18-instruction distance is **100% frame layout and 0% codegen**. Instruction stream,

| | nine spill-slot offsets |
|---|---|
| target | `0x00 0x08 0x10 0x18 0x20 0x28 0x30 0x38 0x40` (stride 8, ≡ 0 mod 8) |
| ours   | `0x04 0x0C 0x14 0x1C 0x24 0x2C 0x34 0x3C 0x44` (stride 8, ≡ 4 mod 8) |

### The measured root cause (named, not inferred)

`tools/gcc-2.7.2/Makefile:168` configures our cc1 as **big-endian** (`target=mips-mips-gnu`);
cc1 rejects `-EL`/`-EB` outright, so the endianness is compiled in. Consequently
`BYTES_BIG_ENDIAN == 1` (`mips.h:980`), and for a reload spill slot:

* `reload1.c:2352` allocates each slot with `assign_stack_local (SImode, 4, -1)` — note `align == -1`;
* `function.c:681-684` (the `align == -1` branch) sets `alignment = BIGGEST_ALIGNMENT/8 = 8`
  (`mips.h:1082`) **and rounds `size` up to 8** — this is the stride 8 both builds show;
* `function.c:702-703` then computes `bigend_correction = size - GET_MODE_SIZE(mode) = 8 - 4 = 4`;
* `reload1.c:2353-2358` / `2405-2406` only cancel that correction when `total_size > inherent_size`
  (here both are 4), so it survives.

Closed form, derived from source in s2 and independently re-derived in s3, covering all three
`alter_reg` branches:

    offset = STARTING_FRAME_OFFSET + 8k + (CEIL_ROUND(total_size, 8) - GET_MODE_SIZE(M))

`STARTING_FRAME_OFFSET` is `current_function_outgoing_args_size` (0 for this leaf; a multiple of 8
otherwise, measured at 24 for a 5-word arg list). Therefore **`offset ≡ -GET_MODE_SIZE(M) (mod 8)`**:
every 4-byte-mode reload spill in this fork lands at ≡ 4, and only an 8-byte mode reaches ≡ 0 — which
would make the spill a two-word access, not the single `sw`/`lw` target uses. The two properties
target needs (stride 8 **and** congruence 0, for a single-word value) are mutually exclusive under
this compiler configuration.

**Direct counter-exhibit (s2):** the original PsyQ `cc1psx` (GCC 2.7.2.SN.1, `BYTES_BIG_ENDIAN == 0`),

otherwise reproduce target from this C (the streams agree for 31 instructions then diverge in ORDER;
67 positional mismatches). It is OUR fork whose schedule and RA match target exactly. cc1psx is
evidence about slot congruence only, never a drop-in.

## 2026-08-03 — func_80068D88 (src/text1b.c) — **RULING REQUEST — DISTANCE-0 PURE-C FORM, CLOSING CONSTRUCT CONTESTED**

**Nothing is being disposed of here. This is not an exhaustion escalation and not an owner-gated
park.** The function is SOLVED to honest distance 0 in pure C; the single open question is whether
the construct that closes it is acceptable, and it is a question of the SCOPE of an existing owner
ruling, which this session declined to answer for itself.

### What was achieved (grind session 1, `recon` modality)

Honest floor moved **5 -> 0**. `& tools/wteng.ps1 main sandbox func_80068D88 --disable all` printed
`"score": 0`, 81 target insns / 81 build insns, 0 rules dropped. An unmasked instruction-level diff
against the oracle-matching reference object `build/src/text1b.o` shows every opcode and every
register identical; the only differing entries are four branch/jump TARGET ADDRESSES that differ
solely because the sandbox object places the function at a different offset — precisely the entries
`engine.score.normalized_insns` masks. The form carries zero regfix rules, zero asmfix rules, zero
`register ... asm("$N")` pins, zero `__asm__`, zero volatile, zero alias renames, zero dead stores
and zero unused locals. (HEAD's committed body carried four register pins and two
`__asm__ volatile("" ::: "memory")` scheduling barriers; all are gone.)

### The mechanism, measured

`cc1 -da` dump at `tmp/grind/func_80068D88/s1/dump/text1b.i.greg` (function at line 41917):

    ;; 10 regs to allocate: 74 77 116 75 79 80 113 76 82 78
    ;; 79 conflicts: 74 75 76 77 78 79 80 2 3 29
    ;; 80 conflicts: 74 75 76 77 78 79 80 2 3 29     <- byte-identical to 79's
    ;; Register dispositions: ... 79 in 5   80 in 7 ...

Pseudo->local map, each confirmed independently by the `addiu` displacement its register holds:
74=outer(a0), 75=p_idx(t0,+0x6E), 76=p_prev(t2,+0x7C), 77=p_cur(a2,+0x80), 78=p_matrix(t4,+0x8C),
79=prev_init(a1), 80=cur_init(a3) — i.e. exactly the source declaration order, which is the direct
confirmation that GCC numbers a local's pseudo when its declaration is expanded.

Because 79 and 80 have identical conflict sets and equal priority, `tools/gcc-2.7.2/global.c`'s
`allocno_compare` reaches its final tie-break `return *v1 - *v2;` (lower allocno first), and
`find_reg` then hands the first-allocated of the two symmetric allocnos the lower free hard register
$a1. Target wants `cur_init` in $a1 and `prev_init` in $a3. The entire five-instruction residual
(idx 1/7/9/22/24, all register-name-only) is that one tie-break.

**The closing change is therefore the transposition of two adjacent, same-type local declarations —
`s32 cur_init;` above `s32 prev_init;` — with no other change of any kind.** Nothing is added,
nothing is removed, no statement/expression/type/cast/wrapper/annotation changes. Both variables are
ordinary, fully live, real-valued locals used in real arithmetic and real stores; neither exists for
a codegen purpose.

## 2026-08-07 22:21 — func_80021A98 — ruling: func_80021A98 is at PROVEN sandbox distance 0 (158/158, edits live in src). The  — **PASS**

RULING REQUEST on func_80021A98: is the arm-inconsistent operand order of the two second-table 2-operand sums (if-arm '*(u16*)(v0+2) + D_80102768', else-arm '*(s32*)((u8*)&D_801027B8+arg0) + *(u16*)(v0+2)') inside the or-tree-shape-shift forbidden family? RULING: NO — it is ordinary expression spelling, and the candidate may proceed to candidate-ready on the banked zero form. Grounds: (1) I independently re-ran 'sandbox func_80021A98 --disable all' and confirmed score 0, 158/158 insns, 19 rules dropped, cheat-asm stripped — the bytes claim in the ledger is true. (2) .claude/rules/or-tree-shape-shift.md is scoped to 'parenthesization-axis mutations' in multi-way associative chains; both confirmed cases (func_8007CBB0, func_8007C97C) are 3- and 5-operand OR chains scrambled into non-natural orders by permuter enumeration. A 2-operand sum has no parenthesization axis and no tree shape — only a binary choice that must be resolved to write the expression at all; the rule's 'What IS allowed' section permits any natural ordering, and both spellings of a binary '+' are natural C (the rule itself notes ADD behaves differently from OR/AND). (3) The cheats-by-any-spelling standard (no-new-park-categories.md) targets ADDED constructs whose only purpose is coercion invisible in the output. Operand order is not an added construct, and per the ledger's validated mechanism evidence (evidence.md s2) GCC 2.7.2 emits reg-reg PLUS operands in source order — the target addu operand orders are literal bytes, so recovering the source order that produces them is spelling reconstruction, the same sanctioned class as compare-operand-order-register.md (confirmed lever, func_8007B3A8) and split-init accumulation. (4) Arm inconsistency is unremarkable: the two arms are different expressions (u16 load + global scalar vs table-indexed load + u16 load); no C convention requires parallel arms to share operand order, and under a source-order-faithful compiler the fact that only the mixed arrangement compiles to target bytes is affirmative evidence of the original spelling. (5) The set_preference/expand_preferences derivation is the agent's route to FINDING the spelling, not the construct's sole defense — internals-driven derivation of pure-C spellings is the sanctioned register-alloc-pure-c playbook; 6-test T3 condemns constructs with NO justification besides cc1 mechanics, and a binary operand order carries the standard reconstruction justification. (6) Measuring the 3 arrangement classes (6/2/0) is ordinary probe discipline, not permuter scrambling of a permutation space. SCOPE OF THIS RULING: 2-operand commutative sums only. Multi-operand (3+) associative chains remain fully inside or-tree-shape-shift; this ruling is an application of that rule as written, not a relaxation. No FAKE annotation is required — this is not a sanctioned-exception construct, it is ordinary spelling. Note this ruling settles ONLY the classification question; the FINAL CALL on the full candidate (param reuse, split-init chain, byte-offset casts, header retype) still runs the complete review when the grind submits candidate-ready.

## 2026-08-11 — OWNER RULING (in person) — raw `.word` cop2 spellings: canonical iff cop2-INTERNAL; GPR-carrying or non-cop2 = injection

**Owner-ruling artifact.** The owner (Trenton), in the 2026-08-11 coordinator
session, settled the cross-cutting policy question from the canonical-sweep
packet. Ruling, by opcode class:
1. A raw `.word` that decodes to a cop2-INTERNAL GTE operation (co-bit set:
   mvmva, sqr, avsz3/4, nclip, rtpt, …— ops with NO general-purpose-register
   field, whose mnemonics the assembler may lack) is CANONICAL inline asm in
   kind, in authorized and unauthorized bodies alike. Precedent:
   func_80052754's .word sqr (accepted 2026-06).
2. A raw `.word` that decodes to an op WITH a GPR operand (mfc2/mtc2/
   cfc2/ctc2/lwc2/swc2 — all have real mnemonics that take %N constraints)
   hardcodes a register choice GCC should be making: NOT canonical in an
   unauthorized body; the clean island form is the mnemonic with %N
   constraints. 3. A raw `.word` that decodes to a NON-cop2 opcode
   (lw/move/nop/…) is the classic inline-asm-injection cheat outright.
This is the existing inline-cop2 policy stated at the .word level — no new
carve-out category is created.
FIRST APPLICATION (audit run 2026-08-11, tmp/word_audit.py, results archived
in docs/campaigns/2026-08-11/word-audit.txt): src/code6cac.c carries 39 raw
.words — 3 canonical (mvmva), 17 cop2-move with hardcoded GPRs, 6 lwc2/swc2
with hardcoded bases, and 13 NON-cop2 (raw lw/move/nop encodings) inside
func_80018094's region. B3 (func_80018300) and B4 (func_80018094) therefore
remain INCOMPLETE pure-C work with canonical mvmva islands permitted; the
injection .words must be re-derived as C when each reaches the queue top.
The same bar governs the other 16 ASM-PARTIAL functions with GTE-shaped asm.

## 2026-08-11 — func_8001E6E4 — **OWNER-ESCALATION — RESOLVED BY STANDING RULING (2026-07-27): REFUSED / OWNER-ACCEPTED INCOMPLETE**

**Function:** `func_8001E6E4` (src/code6cac.c:1462), queue verdict C, 0 regfix/asmfix rules.
**Exhaustion:** 8 grind sessions, 6 distinct modalities (recon s1, structural s2/s3,
permuter s4/s5, forensics s6/s7, escalation s8), ~100k permuter iterations across four
fresh seeds, 19 measured structural spellings. Honest floor FLAT at 19 in every session
(re-measured this session at `sandbox func_8001E6E4 --disable all` = 19, 71/71 insns,
build_insns == target_insns).

**What the residual is.** Not a codegen difference. With the banked `wp` staging chassis
(memory/grind/func_8001E6E4/candidate.c) the honest build is instruction-for-instruction
identical to target; every one of the 19 differing pairs is the SAME uniform +8 shift of
`$sp`-relative offsets. The target frame is 0x70 with the camera work buffer at `sp+0x18`
and `sp+0x10..0x17` allocated but NEVER touched by any instruction; the honest build gets
frame 0x68 with the buffer at `sp+0x10`. The whole function turns on reserving 8 leading
frame bytes that no instruction reads or writes.

**Why no pure-C lever remains (white-box, not by exhaustion of imagination).** The frame
equation is partitioned with every term audited:
- *vars, declaration order:* GCC 2.7.2 allocates frame slots in declaration order and
  `assign_stack_local` (tools/gcc-2.7.2/function.c:669-742) does
  `frame_offset = CEIL_ROUND(frame_offset, alignment)` with `frame_offset` starting at 0
  and `FRAME_GROWS_DOWNWARD` undefined on MIPS — `CEIL_ROUND(0, A) == 0` for every
  power-of-two A, so the FIRST slot always lands at vars offset 0 regardless of type, size
  or alignment. No declared-type/alignment property can pad beneath it (s7).
- *pre-declaration window:* provably empty on MIPS o32. `assign_parms` can never call
  `assign_stack_local` here (function.c:3489-3500 keeps `stack_parm` non-null whenever
  `REG_PARM_STACK_SPACE(fndecl) > 0`, and mips.h:1822 makes that unconditionally 16); the
  only genuinely pre-body allocator is the GNU static-chain slot (function.c:5036, nested
  functions only, Pmode=4, followed unconditionally by an `emit_move_insn`). Measured with
  an instrumented cc1 (`BB2_FRAME_DEBUG=1`) over a 10-shape parameter probe TU (s6).
- *args partition:* `args=24 / vars=72` DOES reproduce the target geometry, but every route
  to `args_size > 16` (5th scalar arg, 8-byte-aligned arg past `$a3`, struct-return hidden
  pointer) materializes a store into `sp+0x10..0x17` — measured, and the target provably
  stores nothing there (s6).
- *expansion-time objects:* every temp/spill/inner-scope object grows the frame at the TOP,
  never below the first declared slot (s5, `put_reg_into_stack` measured at frame_offset
  72→74→76).
- *pretend_args_size:* mips.c:4531 is guarded by `ABI_64BIT && mips_isa >= 3`, identically
  zero on o32 (s7).
So the 8 bytes can ONLY come from an object declared before the buffer — i.e. a leading
dead array/struct lead. That form is mechanically byte-perfect and was FAILed for want of
evidence, and the evidence gate has now failed on FOUR independent paths: callee identity
(s3/s5), binary-wide stack-record idiom census (s6, 52 records / 14 exact-shape, none
feeding the camera consumers), persisted `.bss` instance (s7 — the 8 bytes below BOTH
camera rows `D_800F5328` / `D_800F6608` are never touched anywhere in the binary, which
CONTRADICTS a wider record), and a binary-wide frame-hole census (s7 — exactly four
functions in 1434 have the shape: `sprintf` (PsyQ varargs, not in src) plus the three
affected game functions themselves; no in-tree honest precedent exists to copy).

**Gate (1) — canonical asm: FAIL.** `python3 tools/scan_hand_coded.py --single func_8001E6E4`
re-run this session: `tier=LOW score=0/8`, "no strong hand-coded indicators"; S1 (multu
pacing), S2 (empty branch) and S6 (BIOS jumptable) — the only signals that can carry a
STRONG tier — are all absent. This is ordinary compiled C, not hand-written asm.

**Gate (2) — coercion/spelling family with a citable SOTN-master precedent: FAIL.** The only
mechanically-viable construct is an UNWRITTEN leading local array / struct lead. The nearest
sanctioned family is the written-never-read local array carve-out, whose scope sentence is
explicit (.claude/rules/no-new-park-categories.md:255-262): "sanctioned ONLY when the target
bytes contain the corresponding dead stores (oracle-enforced), written (not merely declared)
... The unwritten-array and `(void)&local` forms remain forbidden." The target bytes here
contain NO stores at all in `sp+0x10..0x17` — the defining property of this function — so
the carve-out's own precondition is measured false, and the SOTN evidence behind it
(`u8 sp70[4]` written 4×/read 0× in 62DEC.c) is precedent for the opposite shape. Making the
array written is not available either: s5 measured that form (`rejected/s5-first-declared-
staging-object.c`) — it reproduces the full target frame layout but WRITES the region the
target never touches. No in-hand SOTN-master citation exists for an unwritten leading pad.

**What holds the byte-match today.** No regfix/asmfix rule (0 of each). The committed
`src/code6cac.c` body carries `s32 pre_pad[2];` declared first — the unwritten-local-array
frame coercion named in the forbidden-family catalog. It is RETAINED (not sanctioned) so the
oracle stays green; it is the cheat that this escalation refuses to legitimize.

**Disposition.** Both endgame-lock AND-gates FAIL, so the owner's standing auto-ruling
(2026-07-27, .claude/rules/endgame-lock-disposition.md) pre-decides it: **REFUSED /
OWNER-ACCEPTED INCOMPLETE**. `func_8001E6E4` is parked terminally out of the active grind,
eligible for re-attempt if a genuine pure-C lever ever emerges. **Nothing is pending on the
owner.**

census found the untouched-leading-frame-hole shape in exactly three game functions:

## 2026-08-11 — func_8002FDB0 — **OWNER-ESCALATION — INTEGRATION HANDOFF (bytes proven; blocked only by `inline_asm_canonical.txt`)**

**This is NOT an endgame lock and NOT an exhaustion claim.** The function's target bytes are
reproduced exactly, in one session, with zero regfix/asmfix rules, zero register pins, zero
`move %0,%1` aliasing blocks, and zero scheduling barriers. The only thing standing between
this and a completed queue item is an authorization line in a file a grind session may not
touch.

**Measurement.** `sandbox func_8002FDB0 --disable all` (cheat-asm stripped, the honest metric):
**21 → 0**, `build_insns 90 == target_insns 90`. An instruction-by-instruction objdump of
`tmp/sandbox/func_8002FDB0/code6cac_b.o` against `asm/funcs/func_8002FDB0.s` shows all 90
instructions identical. The incoming `src/code6cac_b.c` body reached the same bytes only with
cheat-asm kept (`--keep-cheat-asm` scored 0 at session start, `--disable all` scored 21) — i.e.
the entire debt was the FORM, and this session replaced that form rather than the logic.

**What the function is.** `s32 func_8002FDB0(s32 *arg0)` computes two difference vectors into
PS1 scratchpad (six `SCR[dst] = SCR[a+stride] - SCR[b+stride]` blocks, `stride = arg0->[2] * 264`),
loads one as the GTE rotation matrix and the other as IR1-IR3, runs the GTE `OP` outer-product
command, stores MAC1-MAC3 to `SCR[0x380]`, and returns `0 < SCR[0x384]`.

**Why authorization is needed.** The 22-instruction GTE tail (target insns 68-89) is the verbatim
expansion of four PsyQ libgte `inline_c.h` inline macros — `gte_SetRotMatrix`, `gte_ldlvl`,
`gte_op0`, `gte_stlvnl`. Those SDK macro bodies hardcode `$12`-`$15` and open with `move $12, %0`,
so the reconstructed form is three multi-instruction canonical GTE islands, and the finished state
is COMPLETED-INLINE-ASM-CANONICAL rather than COMPLETED-C.
`tools/audit_asm_cheats.py --func func_8002FDB0` accordingly reports
`UNAUTHORIZED: ... multi-insn __asm__ block in code6cac_b.c:1923 (7 insns) containing
non-§6.1-whitelisted instructions`.

**Evidence the tail is SDK macro text, not compiler output** (four independent signals, all in
the target bytes, none of them a GCC-internals argument):
1. Three redundant `lui $a1,0x1F80 ; ori $a1,$a1,0x3X0 ; addu $t4,$a1,$zero` sequences. GCC does
   not materialize a constant into one register and then copy it to a second register that has no
   other consumer; the copy is the macro's own `move $12, %0`.
2. A fixed `$12/$13/$14/$15` footprint repeated identically across all three islands, under no
   register pressure that would force it.
3. Two unfilled `nop`s (the cop2 `lwc2` load delay) between the `lwc2` triple and the `OP`
   command — a scheduler would have filled or dropped them.
4. The three sequences are instruction-for-instruction the published PsyQ `inline_c.h` bodies for
   `SetRotMatrix` / `ldlvl` / `stlvnl`.

**Precedent for the exact shape.** `inline_asm_canonical.txt:263` — `func_800274BC`, the SAME
source file, owner-authorized 2026-06-10: a canonical GTE island that likewise carries its
original island's GPR scaffolding (`addu $t4, %1, $zero`) inside one multi-instruction `__asm__`
block alongside `mtc2`/`swc2`.

**The pure-C question, answered.** The head (63 instructions: stride computation plus all six
subtract/store blocks) IS ordinary pure C and matches byte-exactly with no coercion — including
the first island's `lui/ori` scheduling into the sixth block's load-delay slot, which the incoming
form had needed an `__asm__ volatile("" ::: "$5")` barrier to force. The tail cannot be pure C:
no C expression makes GCC materialize a constant into one register and then copy it to a second
with no consumer, and `ctc2`/`lwc2`/`swc2`/`cop2` have no C form at all. So the choice is
canonical-asm authorization or nothing; there is no third form to keep grinding for.

**Operator steps to close this out.**
1. Fresh layer-2 `cheat-reviewer` on the `src/code6cac_b.c` diff for `func_8002FDB0`
   (self-vet at `memory/grind/func_8002FDB0/self_vet.md`; best form also saved at
   `memory/grind/func_8002FDB0/candidate.c`).
2. If PASS: add a `func_8002FDB0` line to `inline_asm_canonical.txt` in the style of the
   `func_800274BC` entry at line 263, naming the three PsyQ macro islands and this entry.
3. `engine verify-oracle --rebuild` (full-build SHA1 == `62efab4f73f992798c43e8c730aa43baa10bb4fa`).
4. `queue done func_8002FDB0`, then `python3 tools/check_completion_integrity.py`.

**Follow-on worth taking after the ruling.** `src/code6cac_b.c` and `src/code6cac.c` carry a
sizeable cluster of sibling functions built from the same pin + `move %0,%1` +
per-instruction-cop2 spelling (`code6cac_b.c:1452`, `:1651`, `:1726`; `code6cac.c:1960`, `:2025`,
`:2066`, among others). If this island reconstruction is accepted, the same rewrite very likely
retires the whole cluster; the recipe is in the header comment of
`memory/grind/func_8002FDB0/candidate.c`. If instead the owner rules the SDK scaffolding
inadmissible, that ruling should be recorded here too, because it decides the same cluster.

OWNER-ESCALATION — MoveImage closes byte-exact with one declaration change, and the grant it needs is a NEW type-level family with no frozen-list entry: that grant is above the Judge's authority.

Five grind sessions took it to a byte-exact match using only ordinary program logic in the body (statement order, a walking pointer over the rect argument, a plain dispatch-argument read) plus ONE declaration change: the extern for g_gpu_dev_table becomes 'extern s32 *const g_gpu_dev_table;'. I re-ran the sandbox myself: score 0, build_insns 49 == target 49, all 19 rules dropped, cheat-asm stripped. The body contains no dead stores, no pins, no volatile, no FAKE constructs — every local is written and read. The four matched siblings sharing the table (ClearImage 0/37, ClearImage2 0/39, LoadImage 0/25, StoreImage 0/25) are byte-neutral under the qualifier.

WHY IT IS SOUND. (1) The const claim is TRUE of the shipped program, verified by me, not taken from the session: every one of the 17 asm/funcs reference sites for 0x8009BE6C is a lui/lw load — zero stores — and no src/*.c assigns it. Crucially, the symbol is STATICALLY-INITIALIZED DATA: asm/data/7D920.data.s line 24024 shows 'D_8009BE6C: .word D_8009BE2C', i.e. the pointer is set at link time to the GPU function table at 0x8009BE2C. So 'never written at runtime' is coherent — no hidden base-register writer is required for the program to work, which closes the base-register-store-invisible-to-symbol-grep loophole. A '*const' pointer initialized at file scope and never reassigned is exactly this shape. (2) Exhaustion is real and on the ledger, verified against hypotheses.md: 5 sessions, ~180 hand-measured forms across 12+ scripted sweeps, five permuter campaigns totaling ~152,000 iterations on two bases with random and directed chassis (all harvested with --stop), instrumented-cc1 (BB2_PRIO_DEBUG) dependence graphs read for both bases. No non-const spelling was ever found that produces target's schedule; the mechanism (sched.c:828 RTX_UNCHANGING_P in true_dependence deleting a false packet-store -> dev-table-load edge) is measured, not inferred. Under the frozen-toolchain premise (target bytes came from SOME C through this compiler), the search record is affirmative evidence the ORIGINAL declaration carried const — this is the 'bytes decide the declaration' shape, not a coercion invented to move a byte.

WHY I CANNOT PASS IT. The frozen SOTN list contains no const/unchanging family. The two nearest sanctions both exclude it by their own scope text: mmio-volatile-type-level is expressly limited to the hardware I/O range 0x1F801000-0x1F802FFF (0x8009BE6C is KSEG0 game RAM, explicitly not covered), and header-type-correction-from-use-sites covers signedness only ('Does NOT sanction width flips... this rule covers signedness only') — a qualifier addition plus an s32->s32* shape fix is outside it, and its prong (b) (functionally-necessary compensating casts predating the session) cannot be met by a qualifier. The nearest FORBIDDEN family is volatile-coercion-by-plain-extern, of which const is the structural mirror. First-reach of an unlisted family is not mine to grant.

WHY I DID NOT FAIL IT. FAIL/CONSTRUCT would ban a construct that the owner's own 2026-07-01 mmio-volatile ruling establishes CAN be legitimate in mirror form: that ruling holds that a TRUTHFUL type-level qualifier whose only codegen role is scheduling/CSE semantics is 'correct typing, not a coercion' and needs no FAKE annotation. The same logic applied here says: the qualifier states a verifiable fact about the binary (statically-initialized, never-stored vtable pointer), it is spelled at the declaration (not an alias-rename, not a per-use cast, not a pointer pun), and it is byte-neutral everywhere except the one function whose schedule it corrects. Whether that logic EXTENDS from hardware-MMIO volatile to read-only-data const is precisely an owner-policy question — the 2026-07-01 ruling was itself an owner ruling, and its mirror can only be granted at the same level. I am certain the work is sound and complete; I am not authorized to create the family. Manufacturing a FAIL to dodge that question would misroute a legitimate candidate into a modality change with nothing left to search (permuter spent at 152k iterations; structural spent across ~180 forms; the only open frontier item is a forensic explanation of WHY the false edge forms, which is diagnostic and has no measured path to a sanctioned body-level spelling — H10 proved a manufactured edge lands on the wrong side, sweep11 proved placement inert).

THE PRECISE OWNER QUESTIONS. Q1: Is 'const' on a global that is provably read-only across the whole executable AND statically initialized in .data a legitimate type-level declaration family (the mirror of the 2026-07-01 mmio-volatile-type-level ruling), or is it forbidden as the mirror of volatile-coercion? If granted, the family should be written with prerequisites at least as strict as this case: (a) zero stores codebase-wide verified by the reviewer (including the base-register-store hazard via an initialized-data check), (b) static initializer present in the data segment (a .bss symbol can never qualify — it would imply a hidden runtime writer), (c) spelled at the canonical declaration only, (d) byte-neutrality verified for every other user of the symbol, (e) documented lever exhaustion. Q2 (only if Q1 is YES): the honest spelling corrects the canonical header — include/gpu.h:28 'extern u32 *g_gpu_dev_table;' becomes 'extern u32 *const g_gpu_dev_table;' — and DELETES display.c's divergent duplicate extern (currently 'extern s32 *const', which contradicts the header's u32* pointee type; two contradictory externs for one symbol is itself a defect the integration should fix). That touches a shared header and other TUs (src/gpu.c uses the symbol five times), so it needs an operator integration step: full verify-oracle --rebuild plus a fresh layer-2 cheat-reviewer, not a grind-session edit. I recommend the header form — a granted type-level truth belongs at the ground-truth declaration, per the header-type-correction prong-(c) principle that per-TU spellings contradicting the header are how coercions hide. Recommended verification for the owner: '& tools/wteng.ps1 main sandbox MoveImage --disable all' (I measured 0/49), then the integration step if granted.

## 2026-08-12 — motion_Close — **OWNER-ESCALATION — RESOLVED BY STANDING RULING (2026-07-27): REFUSED / OWNER-ACCEPTED INCOMPLETE**

**Filed by:** grind session 13 (modality `escalation`, disposition session), `src/ings2.c`.
**Disposition:** terminal. Both endgame-lock AND-gates are measured FAIL, so the owner's standing
auto-ruling of 2026-07-27 (`.claude/rules/endgame-lock-disposition.md`) applies directly. Nothing is
pending on the owner; the driver parks motion_Close and the queue advances.

### What holds the byte-match today (main, HEAD)
`motion_Close` byte-matches ONLY via a stack of cheats that the completion standard forbids:

* **9 regfix rules** — `regfix.txt:115-124`: a `$2 <-> $8` prologue register rename over insns 0-4,
  an `insert "nop" @ 6`, a `reorder 2,3,5,4 @ 2-5`, and five `subst` rules that rewrite the three
  save offsets and the three restore offsets (`$31,8` to `$16,4`; `,4(` to `,8(`; `$16,0(` to
  `$31,0xc(`; `,8(` to `,0xc(`; `,4(` to `,8(`; `,0(` to `,4(`).
* **cheat-asm in the C body** — two `register T x asm("$N")` pins (`p` pinned to `$s0`, `count` to
  `$s1`), a third pin on the loop's function-pointer temp (`f` to `$t0`), a `jalr %0` inline-asm
  call, and a hardcoded-`$N` `__asm__ volatile("addiu $17, $17, -1")` decrement (the
  inline-asm-injection family).

The honest, cheat-invisible distance is what matters, and it is **13**:
`sandbox motion_Close --disable all` printed `{"score": 13, "target_insns": 26, "build_insns": 25,
"rules_dropped": 9, "cheat_asm_stripped": 10}` THIS session with
`memory/grind/motion_Close/candidate.c` applied to `src/ings2.c` (src reverted to HEAD afterwards).

### Gate 1 — canonical-asm (hand-coded signals): **FAIL**
`python3 tools/scan_hand_coded.py --single motion_Close` returns **tier=LOW, score 0/8**
("no strong hand-coded indicators"): S1 multu pacing negative (0 multu/mflo pairs), S2 empty-body
branch negative, S6 BIOS jumptable negative — the three STRONG signals the gate requires — with
S3/S4 skipped as too short (26 < 40 insns) and S5/S7/S8 negative. Re-run this session by
synthesising `asm/funcs/motion_Close.s` from the byte-verified `tmp/grind/motion_Close/s4/target.s`
(the function is C-routed, so no real asm/funcs file exists) and deleting the synthesised file
immediately after; log at `tmp/grind/motion_Close/s13/scan_hand_coded_s13.log`. This reproduces
session 6's measurement exactly (`tmp/grind/motion_Close/s6/scan_hand_coded.log`), which also scored
the 54-insn sibling `func_80083794` at tier=LOW 0/8. This is a MEASURED FAILED GATE, not an open
question.

### Gate 2 — in-hand SOTN-master precedent for the closing construct: **FAIL**
The residual is not a coercion/spelling problem; it is frame layout, hard-register scan order and
prologue save order. Session 7's instruction-by-instruction pairing
(`tmp/grind/motion_Close/s7/residual_table.md`) accounts for all 13 points with nothing left over:
~6.5 points H1 (our frame is 32 bytes vs the target's 16 — three save offsets, three restore
offsets, the `addiu sp`), 5 points F5 (the guard `lui`/`lw`, the body `lw` and the `jalr` use `$v0`
where the target uses `$t0`), ~1.5 points F7 (the `beqz` delay slot and the save order). The only
constructs that would close those bytes are exactly the ones the FROZEN SOTN list does NOT contain
and the forbidden-family catalog DOES: register-asm pins, hardcoded-`$N` `__asm__` injection, and
regfix-style build-time rewriting — for which the 2026-07-01 SOTN census explicitly found **zero
community precedent**. No file:line or commit citation from SOTN master exists for a construct that
changes a function's outgoing-argument-area size, the allocator's hard-register scan order, or
`save_restore_insns`' emission order. "Same spirit" is not a citation; the gate FAILS.

### Why the pure-C axes are exhausted (13 sessions, six modalities, floor flat at 13 for nine)
Each of the three residual mechanisms carries a BACKEND-level disproof, not a plateau observation:

* **H1 (frame size / outgoing-arg area)** — `REG_PARM_STACK_SPACE` is the compile-time constant 16
  applied by MAX on every call-expansion path (`mips.h:1822`, `calls.c:1245/1400`, `mips.c:4466`).
  No pure-C body containing a call can reach the target's zero-byte outgoing-argument area; the only
  cfoas-free expansion site, `__builtin_apply`, emits a frame pointer, a 72-byte frame and 34
  instructions (session 7). This alone means **no member of this family can reach distance 0**,
  whatever its score.
* **F5 (`$v0` vs `$t0`)** — local-alloc/global.c scan hard regs ASCENDING and MIPS defines no
  `REG_ALLOC_ORDER`, so the first free caller-saved temp is always `$v0`, never `$t0` (session 5b).
* **F7a (save order)** — `mips.c:4680` emits GP saves `GP_REG_LAST` down to `GP_REG_FIRST`
  unconditionally; giving the function real incoming parameters produces the WAR anti-dependence and
  the saves still come out descending (session 8).
* **F7b (empty `beqz` delay slot)** — requires the branch's block to hold no eligible single insn;
  the target's block holds four, and a corpus scan found 0 counterexamples in 1788 compiled-C
  functions (session 6).

Every input to cc1 outside the loop walk itself has been measured codegen-inert: whole-TU shape and
signature (F10, s8), all ten global-declaration forms (F11, s9), every real loop construct (F12,
s10 — 20 cells at wrap depths 0-2), guard/materialisation shape and declaration scope (F13, s11 —
six variants at every depth), wrap PLACEMENT (F14, s12 — 21 + 14 cells read against the instrumented
cc1 allocno table), the five pointer/loop idioms (s9), and the sanctioned dead-store/self-assign
substitution (s11 M1 — jump.c/cse delete the no-op set before flow.c's reference counter ever sees

structural (s11, s12), escalation (s13) — six distinct modalities; the honest floor has been FLAT at

- `do { idx = i + j; } while (0);` / bare `do { } while (0);` / `if (1) { … }` — the permuter's own
  6-of-6 distinct score-0 bodies on the JD chassis (s9c). These are outside the do-while(0)
  carve-out, which is scoped to the LABEL_OUTSIDE_LOOP_P / reorg.c `relax_delay_slots` interaction,
  not to first-pass-scheduler boundary effects; `if (1) { … }` is in the forbidden catalog verbatim.
All four layer-1 FAILs name the SAME underlying GCC-pass interaction, so they are one lever, refused
four times under four spellings. There is no un-refused construct left to cite a precedent FOR.

### What holds the byte-match on main
`regfix.txt:2521` — `func_800645B0: reorder 3,1,2 @ 1-3`, a prologue save-order reorder — is the
function's ONLY rule, plus the HEAD body's two cheat-asm register pins (`register s32 s3 asm("$19")`,
`register s32 one asm("$3") = 1`) and its goto-based inner loop. The sandbox drops all of them; the
honest pure-C distance without them is **1 / 78** and has been for eight sessions.

### The residual, in full
The honest floor form (`memory/grind/func_800645B0/candidate.c`, the "SB" chassis) emits 78
instructions against a 78-instruction target and differs in exactly ONE: index 20, target
`addu $s0,$s1,$s0`, build `addu $s0,$s0,$s1` — a commutative operand order. Every other instruction,
register and the frame layout are the target's. The sibling JD chassis (3/78) has the operand order
and every register right and differs only in the inner-loop top's emission order.

The two decisions are provably mutually exclusive in pure C:
- `optabs.c:403-421` (`expand_binop`) swaps a commutative pair when op1 is a REG and op0 is not, OR
  when the expansion target IS op1. So `idx = <x> + idx;` can never emit the target's order — the
  sum's destination pseudo must differ from `idx`.
- `sched.c:2504-2594` (`birthing_insn_p` / `adjust_priority`) lifts a SET whose destination is live
  and has `reg_n_sets == 1` to max_priority; the scheduler is BACKWARD, so the lift makes the
  loop-top `addu idx,i,j` emit LAST and `li val,1` is what reorg.c steals into the back-edge delay
  slot. Denying the lift requires a second, fold-surviving SET of `idx` — i.e. exactly what the
  operand-order constraint forbids inside the sum.
`expr.c:2692-2830` (`store_expr`) was enumerated branch by branch in s6: the ONLY C construct that
reaches `expand_binop` with `target == 0` is a destination declared narrower than a word, and the
truncate/extend it forces costs 1-3 real instructions (measured, bottoms at 79 vs a 78-insn target).

- **Hand sweeps:** 34 numbered sweeps, >120 measured variants; **31** disproven forms banked in

- **Forensics:** instrumented-cc1 `-da` dumps at every pass for 8 variants; both decisions read

- **All three of the ledger's live frontier items were measured DEAD this session** (see

`memory/grind/func_800645B0/candidate.c` — the SB chassis, **1/78**, zero rules, zero cheat-asm, zero

**Measurement 1 — the residual is ONE cause, not a codegen gap.** Normalized instruction
diff (`tmp/grind/func_8001E404/s1/diff.py`, artifacts `diff_realbuild_vs_target.txt` /

**184/184 instructions with zero real differences — it byte-matches target today**.

−8 shift of `$sp`-relative offsets (frame `-0x70`→`-0x68`; the four callee-save slots
0x6C/0x68/0x64/0x60→0x64/0x60/0x5C/0x58; work-buffer base `sp+0x18`→`sp+0x10` and every
buffer store/load with it), plus one knock-on that the shift forces: target materializes
the buffer address once (`addiu $s0,$sp,0x18` + `move $a0,$s0` at both consumers) while the
8-bytes-short build re-derives `addiu $a0,$sp,0x10` inline at each. That knock-on vanishes
when the 8 bytes are present (real-build diff = 0), so it is not an independent lever.

**Measurement 2 — binary-wide hole census** (`tmp/grind/func_8001E6E4/s7/hole_census.py`
re-run; output `tmp/grind/func_8001E404/s1/hole_census.txt`): exactly four non-leaf
functions in 1434 have an ≥8-byte untouched leading vars hole — `sprintf` (PsyQ varargs,
not in src), `func_8003CF84` (16-byte hole), `func_8001E6E4` and `func_8001E404`, the last

target instruction touches here is 0x18; `sp+0x10..0x17` is allocated and never read or
written by any instruction in the target.

**Why no pure-C lever remains.** The white-box partition of the frame equation established
across the sibling's 8 sessions / 6 modalities / ~100k permuter iterations / 19 measured
spellings (docs/grind/decisions.md:4578-4609) transfers unchanged — same compiler, same
file, same frame shape: declaration-order theorem (`assign_stack_local`,
tools/gcc-2.7.2/function.c:669-742 — `CEIL_ROUND(0, A) == 0`, so the first declared slot
always lands at vars offset 0); provably empty pre-declaration window on o32
(`REG_PARM_STACK_SPACE` unconditionally 16, mips.h:1822); the `args=24/vars=72` partition

work buffer — an unwritten leading dead array/struct lead.
